<!-- pr-reviewer: 83ec867ee46e508a67cede40b76ac36e5012f2b6 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good
- The change is small. In `crates/app/src/posting_serves.rs:60` the door reads an explicit `serves` list first. If none exists, `voices_wire_edm()` makes the script serve only `Kind::WireEdm`.
- No refusal is dropped. Registry posts and explicit `serves` lists run before the new branch and are not changed. A cutting script is still refused on a wire EDM by name. An undeclared script is still refused on plasma and sinker.
- One side effect, which is correct: a user script with `wireEdm = true` and no `serves` is now refused on a Mill, Lathe and MillTurn. Before, the milling mask admitted it there. This makes the door stricter.
- The flag comes from the engine's strict boolean reading. The pins cover `false`, `1` and `"true"`.
- The decision file is present. No dependency, golden or PNG changes. No process files are touched.

Results (merged with main, locally; no runner or Actions run)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib serves`: 3 passed (the three new pins).
- `post_serves_kind`: 6 passed. `post_serves_plasma`: 1 passed. `edm_machine`: 5 passed. `edm_conditions`: 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Mutation check: I changed the wire branch to `return Ok(true);`. `user_wire_manifest_serves_only_wire_edm` failed (tests.rs:15, a Mill was admitted). The other two pins still passed, as expected. I restored the code.

Not exercised
- No real control ran on actual G-code. The pins call the admission and refusal functions directly. No posted wire EDM program was generated or read here, and no physical EDM or UI picker was used.
- Windows-only `cfg` arms: the diff has none.

Requested before merge
- None.

Questions / notes (not blocking)
- The `Script::load` call parses the script a second time in this door. This is a small cost on a non-hot path.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
